players.product: Carbonate fuel-cell power plants (FuelCell Energy Blocks) for behind-the-meter baseload data-center power

quarterly_data.signal: FuelCell Energy's Q2 FY2026 results (8-K, quarter ended April 30, 2026): revenue $35.6 million versus $37.4 million (-5%) - product $18,018 thousand (module deliveries to customers in Korea), service $4,175 thousand (no module exchanges), generation $8,681 thousand (Groton Project under repair), Advanced Technologies $4,715 thousand. Gross loss $(12.9) million; Adjusted EBITDA $(17.1) million versus $(19.3) million; net loss $(77.6) million, driven by a $42.6 million impairment tied to upgrading the Groton Project to three standard 2.5 MW FCE Blocks.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 FY2026 revenue $35.6 million (-5%); Adjusted EBITDA $(17.1) million

quarterly_data.signal: Backlog was $1.14 billion as of April 30, 2026 versus $1.26 billion (-9.9%): product $36,115 thousand, service $155,350 thousand, generation $928,482 thousand, Advanced Technologies $15,440 thousand. Sales pipeline: 4 GW of proposals delivered in Q2 2026 (over 5 GW year to date in FY2026), a 267% increase in total pipeline from Q1 2026; data centers account for about 90% of the pipeline and average proposal size doubled ('2x increase') from Q1. The pipeline is ongoing commercial discussions, not signed agreements.
quarterly_data.figure: backlog $1.14 billion (-9.9%); 4 GW of Q2 proposals; pipeline +267% QoQ; data centers ~90%

quarterly_data.signal: FuelCell introduced a standardized 12.5 MW FuelCell Energy Block for data centers, combining 10 of its 1.25 MW modules to reduce repeat engineering and permitting and speed multi-MW deployments in grid-constrained markets. CEO Jason Few: 'we are focused on extending the grid to the data center'. Deck figures (company operating experience and design targets): electrical efficiency 50% in 2026 versus 46% in 2003, 7-year stack life design, native DC output, 99% system availability, up to 33 MW per acre, 90% U.S.-based suppliers.
quarterly_data.figure: 12.5 MW FuelCell Energy Block (10 x 1.25 MW modules); 50% electrical efficiency

quarterly_data.signal: In light of increased demand the previously contemplated Torrington, CT expansion to an annualized production rate of up to 350 MW was raised to a target of up to 500 MW, estimated to cost $200 to $275 million and to be executed over the next twenty four months; as of May 31, 2026 installation of a new high-volume tape caster had begun and a new conditioning room had been commissioned. Fiscal 2026 growth spending of $20-$30 million for the expansion was on track. The deck's later phases add a global assembly footprint beyond 500 MW and new high-volume cell manufacturing facilities (500 MW - 1 GW+), to be built when supported by market demand.
quarterly_data.figure: expansion target raised from up to 350 MW to up to 500 MW ($200-$275 million, 24 months)
